messages:
maria: FYI escalation from AcmeCorp — they see intermittent 500s and +400ms tail latency.
Console shows region: ap-southeast-1, but their response headers/traces show requests served from us-west-2. Customer worried about cost + latency.

maria: repro curl they sent:
```bash
curl -i -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-***\" \\
  -H \"x-client-id: acme-frontend\" \\
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{\"prompt\":\"hi\"}'
```
response headers (from customer trace):
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
x-request-id: req_6a2f9
x-serving-region: us-west-2
x-routing-decision: fallback-to-compatible
content-length: 512
```
They also attached a short trace showing 430ms added RTT compared to requests served from ap-southeast-1.

devon: can you paste the full x-request-id and the time window? need to look up routing logs. also did they send the console screenshot that shows ap-southeast-1? :eyes:

maria: request id is req_6a2f9 (they included a list; sending the one with 500s: req_6a2f9-3). Issue appears starting 2024-10-18 09:12 UTC.
Screenshot attached showing "Serving region: AP-SG" on console for that customer account.

oliver: infra note — we had a short capacity pressure incident in ap-southeast-1 at 09:10 UTC, auto-fallbacks were triggered to us-west-2 and eu-west-1 for some routes. normally the console label is derived from account.primary_pop but routing can fallback to compatible pops. we should expect x-serving-region to reflect actual serving pop (which matches customer headers).

sasha: platform check — console UI pulls last-known primary_pop from config-sync service. there was a config-sync job failure during the 09:00 deploy; primary_pop was not refreshed for a subset of accounts, so UI kept showing AP-SG even when routing sent to US-W.

route-bot: [automated] deploy: config-sync v2.7.3 failed healthcheck 2024-10-18T09:03:12Z, rollback initiated 09:04:08Z. Impact: partial primary_pop bloom update skipped for ~2k accounts.

devon: ok — so two issues: (1) routing correctly fell back to us-west-2 due to capacity, (2) console label was stale because config-sync missed update. Need to confirm why fallback decisions also set x-routing-decision header ":fallback-to-compatible" instead of the fallback-policy id — that makes reconciling billing harder.

maria: customer also reports some 500s. sample error payload they sent:
```
{"time":"2024-10-18T09:12:22Z","request":"req_6a2f9-3","error":"upstream timeout","status":502}
```
They say errors occurred only when routed to us-west-2; when we forced them back to ap-sg they were fine.

oliver: infra — there was transient fullness on the us-west-2 fallback pool later at 09:12 which caused the occasional 502s. we should correlate routing logs and serving infra metrics. i'll pull the scheduler events for req_6a2f9-3.

sasha: short-term mitigation: (1) ask customer to set header `x-preferred-pop: ap-southeast-1` or add `region_pin=true` in the API payload to avoid fallbacks, (2) we'll patch console to show a tooltip clarifying that the UI shows primary_pop and actual serving pop is visible via response headers and request logs.

maria: sending workaround + repro steps to customer now with sample curl they can try:
```bash
curl -i -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-***\" \\
  -H \"x-preferred-pop: ap-southeast-1\" \\
  -H \"x-client-id: acme-frontend\" \\
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{\"prompt\":\"hi\",\"region_pin\":true}'
```
Please confirm latency/500s.

customer (via support note): after adding header, latency dropped back to ~60ms. still saw 1x 500 in the next 30m. billing dashboard shows a chunk of these requests billed at US prices (they're concerned).

devon: for billing reconciliation — routing logs include actual serving pop and cost tier. if console metrics were aggregated by primary_pop for that window, that explains the mismatch. we need to run a reconciliation job to re-attribute usage by x-serving-region for 09:00-09:30 UTC for affected accounts.

oliver: i'll open infra ticket INF-4828 to collect scheduler traces + pool fullness graphs and run the reconciliation. tagging finance.

route-bot: [automated] ticket INF-4828 created by oliver at 2024-10-18T10:04:22Z. assigned: infra.

sasha: action items:
- infra (oliver): pull scheduler events and confirm root cause of 502s + capacity timeline
- platform (devon): add a short-term UI patch clarifying label vs serving-pop and make routing header clearer (`x-routing-policy-id`)
- support (maria): send customer remediation and ask for a week of logs if anything recurs
- billing/finance: reconcile costs for customer for 2024-10-18T09:00-09:30 UTC if re-attribution needed

maria: noted, will update customer thread and follow up when recon is done. :thumbsup:"
